definition: the record behind what we cannot talk about, as I actually stated it

settled:
The set of topics that I expect to be safe and the set of topics that I care about are disjoint. Sometimes I stumble into an unexpected intersection, but it is not predictable.

If a topic is safe for Jen, it is almost always either not interesting for me or not interesting for her. If a topic is interesting for me, it is almost always either not interesting for Jen or not safe for her.

About fifty-eight percent of what I focus on sits outside both her alignment and standard social alignment, which is why the intersection is small enough to feel empty.

Correcting a guess that maths would be the worst: maths is not the one she is most threatened by. I think the confirmed misalignment is an even more threatening case for her than the implied misalignment that comes from not understanding.

On the length of a wave: six weeks is pretty normal.

On why it is a variable schedule: our conversations only go well when both of us have high capacity. It is almost never easy.

title: The Disjoint Sets In My Words
